body:
As there is not reproducer, could you please help me to debug the context creation? I have runnable jar from a bad and a good build.

I've updated to quarkus 2.7.1 in the meanwhile.

>  then runner.jar produced sometimes contains duplicated instances of the given bean.

How do you detect a "duplicated instance"?

> As there is not reproducer, could you please help me to debug the context creation? I have runnable jar from a bad and a good build.

Have you tried to log the stack trace inside the `@PostConstruct` callback? I'm not sure if a "runnable jar" is something that would help us.

I'm printing the identityhashcodes at various locations (constructor, startup event etc)
I'll add stack traces as wel.

I'm using the quarkus maven plugin to construct the runnable application. 
This is referencing various other projects only, there is no code or resources in that particular project.

> I'm printing the identityhashcodes at various locations (constructor, startup event etc)
> I'll add stack traces as wel.

Ok, more info would be really helpful.

> I'm printing the identityhashcodes at various locations (constructor, startup event etc)

Constructor you say? Because you're using an Interceptor (`@ActivateRequestContext` is an InterceptorBinding), there is likely at least one subclass of your singleton class to implement the proxy pattern that is necessary for that to work. That generated subclass must, of course, call some constructor of your class (the no-arg constructor to be specific). If I were to guess, I'd say that your two instances are the contextual instance of your class (i.e. the "real" instance of your singleton) and the proxy instance of the subclass.

Try putting a print-statement into the `@PostConstruct` method. In contrast to the constructor, that should only get executed once and only on the contextual instance.

I'm not sure what's up with the startup event you mentioned. Is the observer method an instance method or a static method? Quarkus' Interceptors work differently in these cases, I believe.

I noticed the SubClass therefore the println was added to the event handlers and the post construct calls.

In case the build creates a wrong jar then I see two beans, in case it is good, then I only see one. The difference is only that it was compiled 5 minutes later.

I'm working on adding stacktraces to the binaries. Unfortunately the odds of having such build is low, therefore I'll have to monkey patch them or add it using byteman or so.

After upgrade to  2.7.1, the problem still occurs. Today the problem was more apparent, three times in a row wrong context was created:

Stacktrace for the constructor and postconstruct calls:
[ngbpdemo_backend_1_bad_stacktrace.log](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/files/8132134/ngbpdemo_backend_1_bad_stacktrace.log)

After compiling only one of the modules and just recompile the runner, then the problem disappeared, even if the full project was built. Maybe there is a correlation between available memory, because it *seems* that the problem is more frequent in case the IDE is not running. 

This is how the same context and same source looks like with a good build:
[ngbpdemo_backend_1_jo1.log](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/files/8132133/ngbpdemo_backend_1_jo1.log)

> After compiling only one of the modules and just recompile the runner, then the problem disappeared, even if the full project was built. 

Hm, what does your app structure look like? Is it a multi-module project? Is `adapter.giro.workers.SendEventHandlerWorker` placed in a dependency or in the application itself, i.e. `src/main/java`?

In case you get two beans created, is one of them ever destroyed? I.e. if you add a pre destroy callback, will it be invoked for one of them? Will the context be activated/deactivated multiple times (it definitely shouldn't be the case for singleton, I am just really shooting blind here).
Also, you mentioned that the bean has an observer for startup event - what's the chronological order of the dual bean creation and this event? Does one of them get notified, do both?
